what_it_does: In chip design, a clock tree is the network of wires and signal-booster components (buffers) that distributes a precise timing pulse to every part of the chip so all circuits work in sync. As chips shrink, designers are now starting to route clock wires on both the front face and the back face of the silicon wafer, but existing tools only know how to handle one side. This paper introduces a systematic method for building these double-sided clock trees, jointly optimizing several competing goals — signal delay, timing skew (how much the clock pulse drifts between different parts of the chip), total wire length, and the number of vias (vertical holes that connect front to back). The routing relies on tiny vertical connectors called nano Through-Silicon Vias (nTSVs) that punch through the wafer to link the two wiring layers.
